newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton down on low mill buys, new arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton down on low mill buys, new arrivals.

text.p: Cotton prices extended losses on the local market on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Mill buying was low while rising new crop arrivals dragged prices downward," one dealer said.
Millers kept to the sidelines, expecting further price erosion, and sentiment was subdued in limited activity.
"Last week arrivals were low in the Punjab region ahead of assembly election but now elections are over and arrivals have picked up again," one broker said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi fell by five rupees to 770/800 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).

Punjab saw-ginned fell ten rupees at 1,380/1,600 rupees per maund. F-414 slid by ten rupees at 1,770/1,790 rupees per maund. Gujarat cotton on the other hand moved in a narrow range and settled on a quiet note.
